highlights.title: Introducing Claude Opus 5
highlights.summary: Anthropic has announced Claude Opus 5, the latest and most capable model in the Claude lineup. Developers using Claude Code should explore how this new model can enhance their coding workflows, as it likely brings improvements in reasoning, code generation, and complex task handling.

highlights.title: Auto Mode is Now the Default in Claude Code
highlights.summary: Anthropic has made Auto mode the default behavior in Claude Code, meaning the tool now automatically selects the best model and approach for each task without manual configuration. This is a big win for beginners who no longer need to worry about choosing settings — just start coding and let Claude decide.

highlights.title: Message Your Other Claude Code Sessions
highlights.summary: Claude Code now supports cross-session messaging, allowing you to send messages between different active Claude Code sessions. This is powerful for developers running parallel tasks — for example, one session could notify another when a build finishes or a subtask is complete.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.224 Released — Self-Hosted Runners & Archive Plugins
highlights.summary: Version 2.1.224 introduces self-hosted environments via `claude self-hosted-runner`, letting teams run Claude Code sessions on their own machines or containers under Team and Enterprise plans. It also adds an `archive` plugin source so you can install plugins directly from a zip file over HTTPS without needing git.

highlights.title: Claude Code v2.1.227 Released — Feature Flag & Bash Action Fixes
highlights.summary: This patch fixes a bug where feature flags were evaluated without checking the user's subscription tier when a session started with an expired login token, which could incorrectly prompt Max plan users to enable usage credits. It also resolves an issue causing every Bash command to fail when using `claude-code-action`.

highlights.title: Claude Code Tutorial: Beginner to Pro In 15 Minutes
highlights.summary: This YouTube tutorial promises to take you from zero to productive with Claude Code in just 15 minutes, making it ideal for developers who want a quick but comprehensive introduction. It's a great starting point if you're new to AI-assisted coding and want to understand the core workflow fast.

highlights.title: Agent Skills That Bring Team Coding Standards to Claude Code
highlights.summary: This open-source project provides reusable agent skills that enforce team coding standards inside Claude Code, helping organizations keep AI-generated code consistent with their conventions. If your team struggles with Claude producing code that doesn't match your style guide or architecture patterns, this is worth exploring.

highlights.title: Mastering Claude Code in 30 Minutes
highlights.summary: A focused 30-minute YouTube tutorial designed to help developers move beyond the basics and build real proficiency with Claude Code. This is a solid next step after you've tried Claude Code a few times and want to learn power-user techniques and best practices.

tips_of_the_day: Take advantage of Auto mode being the new default — instead of spending time tuning model settings, write a clear, detailed prompt describing your task and let Claude Code pick the best approach automatically.

If you run multiple Claude Code sessions for large projects, try cross-session messaging to coordinate subtasks: kick off a long-running build in one session and have it signal your main session when it's done, keeping your workflow unblocked.

When installing Claude Code plugins for your team, use the new `archive` plugin source to distribute internal plugins as a zip over HTTPS — no git server required, making it much easier to share private tooling in corporate environments.
